stories.title: Aurora eyes growth with IA Capital investment
stories.summary: Aurora, an MGA and algorithmic underwriting-as-a-service business, has secured investment from IA Capital Group to fund its next phase of growth under Co-founder and CEO Bijal Patel. Its model is already live in production with QBE Insurance, and in March 2026 it launched QBE's British Marine Yacht Protection & Indemnity (P&I) product, cutting quote-to-bind time from days to under 10 minutes. Rick Viton of IA Capital Group and James Orchard, CEO of QBE Ventures, have been appointed to Aurora's board, and the firm plans to re-platform as AI-native and scale across more products and insurers.
stories.why_it_matters: Outside investment and a live QBE deployment show algorithmic underwriting being backed as a way for insurers to quote faster on specialty lines while keeping pricing consistent.

stories.title: Lancashire enters cat bond market seeking $175m S6 Re aggregate peak peril retro
stories.summary: Lancashire Holdings has entered the catastrophe bond market for the first time, seeking $175 million of multi-year collateralised aggregate peak peril retrocession through its debut S6 Re Limited (Series 2027-1) notes. The single Class A tranche would fully collateralise a retrocession agreement with Lancashire Insurance Company, covering it and other Lancashire subsidiaries over a five year term on an annual aggregate and weighted industry loss index trigger. The covered perils are North America named storm, North America earthquake, Japan earthquake, Japan typhoon and European windstorm.
stories.why_it_matters: A long-standing London and Lloyd's market underwriter turning to cat bond investors for five-year annual aggregate retro shows capital markets taking a bigger role in peak peril protection.

stories.title: Shares in London-listed Anthropic investors rise ahead of blockbuster IPO
stories.summary: London-listed tech trusts with stakes in Anthropic rose on Wednesday morning after Nvidia's earnings lifted sentiment towards the AI sector. Anthropic is due to debut on the Nasdaq in less than 24 hours, seeking to raise as much as $90.4bn at a $1.4 trillion (£1.1 trillion) valuation, with shares nearly seven times oversubscribed. Nvidia reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.68 against expectations of $2.47, and data centre revenue up 110 per cent to $107.6bn, while Baillie Gifford US Growth Trust rose 1.5 per cent to 347p and Scottish Mortgage Investment Trust rose 1.6 per cent.
stories.why_it_matters: Strong Nvidia results lifted the trusts, but further gains now depend on Anthropic's debut meeting very high expectations, so UK holders carry concentrated AI exposure.

The scale of Healey’s inflation problem is coming into full view
stories.summary: UK inflation rose to 3.6 per cent in the year to October, further above the Bank of England's two per cent target. Food inflation softened and core inflation was little changed from September's reading, while oil prices remain above $90 per barrel. Cornwall Insight warned the energy price cap would rise by £443 in January, taking annualised household energy bills to £2,166, and the Bank expects inflation to keep rising for at least another half year.
stories.why_it_matters: Energy-led inflation that stays well above target limits how far the Bank of England can cut rates, which affects gilt yields, mortgage costs and sterling.
stories.access_note: UK retail investors can get exposure through gilts held directly, bond ETFs, index-linked gilts, sterling FX, and spread bets or CFDs on rates, FX and oil.

stories.title: Xi personally welcomes Trump to China for high-stakes summit
stories.summary: President Donald Trump was welcomed on the tarmac in Shenzhen on Wednesday by Chinese President Xi Jinping, which is historically extremely rare for China's top leader. Trump is due to hold bilateral talks with Xi on Thursday, then join Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin for a trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, the first time the three have met together. Topics include a new framework for nuclear arms control after the last U.S.-Russia nuclear arms treaty expired in February, and the Iran war, though U.S. officials describe the talks as an opening conversation and expectations for breakthroughs are low.
stories.why_it_matters: A first three-way meeting between the US, China and Russia could shape arms control and the Iran war, but low expectations limit the scope for near-term market-moving outcomes.

stories.title: France’s Philippe steps up attacks on Le Pen and Mélenchon as his poll numbers slide
stories.summary: Centre-right presidential hopeful Edouard Philippe sharpened his attacks on rivals Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon in a speech on Wednesday, accusing both of an “unhealthy fascination” with Vladimir Putin and of economic plans that could push France into a financial crisis. Polls now show Le Pen and Mélenchon advancing to the runoff next spring, while Philippe, Gabriel Attal and Bruno Retailleau have lost ground. Attal, Retailleau and David Lisnard agreed on Tuesday to hold a primary in January with a few televised debates, but have not agreed on who should take part, and Philippe says he will not join a contest that would likely deepen divisions.
stories.why_it_matters: Polls pointing to a far-right versus far-left runoff, with moderates divided, raise the prospect of France's costly fiscal proposals shaping the 2027 race and French debt sentiment.

stories.title: Typical energy bill forecast to go up by £443 a year from January as inflation rate rises again
stories.summary: Energy bills are expected to jump by 26% a year for a typical household. The headline puts the rise at £443 a year from January. It comes as UK inflation hits its highest rate for a year.
stories.why_it_matters: Higher household energy costs add to the inflation pressure that is already rising, which bears on household budgets and on the outlook for UK prices.

stories.title: Who to watch in Spain's election race
stories.summary: Spain votes on 29 November. The conservatives are leading most polls. This follows eight years of Socialist-led rule.
stories.why_it_matters: A win for the conservatives would end eight years of Socialist-led government in Spain, a change of direction that markets and investors with European exposure may watch.

market_idea.title: Inflation hedge using index-linked gilts
market_idea.what_the_trade_is: The view is that UK inflation, at 3.6 per cent in the year to October, will keep rising for at least another half year, as the Bank of England expects, with energy bills set to climb in January. The position aims to protect against, or profit from, inflation running above what is expected.
market_idea.how_it_is_expressed: An outright position in inflation-linked bonds, whose payments rise with inflation, is a simple form of hedge. The same view can be expressed against conventional bonds, which lose value in real terms when inflation is higher.
market_idea.retail_access: A UK retail investor could use index-linked gilts held directly, or ETFs holding inflation-linked bonds. Gilts held directly are generally free of capital gains tax, whereas spread bets and CFDs use leverage and margin, which magnify losses as well as gains.
market_idea.what_makes_it_work: Inflation needs to come in higher than the level already priced into index-linked bonds, which would raise their returns relative to conventional bonds.
market_idea.what_breaks_it: If energy prices fall and inflation eases faster than expected, or real yields rise, the bonds could lose value.
market_idea.disclaimer: An explanation of a trade in the news, not a recommendation.
